subject.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets

question: Should `models auth clear-cooldown <profile-id>` become OpenClaw’s supported explicit operator recovery action for early provider/billing recovery, or should recovery instead be guided through Doctor/UI or automatic probing?
rationale: The patch can be assessed mechanically, but adding a public command that clears persisted provider eligibility is a durable UX and compatibility contract choice rather than a purely internal bug repair.

options.title: Adopt the explicit command
options.body: Approve the profile-scoped command as an opt-in escape hatch after redacted live proof shows the blocked state, reset, safe restart, and recovered request.

options.title: Use guided recovery instead
options.body: Pause this PR and move the operator action to Doctor or an in-product recovery surface so a blocked user does not need SQLite knowledge or a manual shell workflow.

options.title: Rely on automatic recovery
options.body: Close the PR if maintainers want billing recovery handled only by automatic probes and fallback policy rather than a public state-reset command.

recommendation.title: Adopt the explicit command
recommendation.body: Approve the profile-scoped command as an opt-in escape hatch after redacted live proof shows the blocked state, reset, safe restart, and recovered request.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal combines major auth-profile refactoring with merger responsibility in the related cooldown-state area.
